worked_solution:
The straight-line solutions of the system have the form

$$
{c}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{c}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=\frac{1}{2}x,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/97f7eb1fbddcd9d927447978efd4c42e705d6835bf0cc74525d42ded8c35346b.png)

The tangents along this line are pointing $\text{away from the origin},$ meaning that the solutions of the form 
${c}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
must approach $\text{infinity}$ as $t\to \infty .$ So, we must have ${\lambda }_{1}>0.$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=-x,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/edc697ab38ae9a56d46181e0a45982b7045224de0cc3c4a786ddbc515f22196c.png)

The tangents along this line are pointing $\text{away from the origin},$ meaning that the solutions of the form 
${c}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
must approach $\text{infinity}$ as $t\to \infty .$ So, we must have ${\lambda }_{2}>0.$

So, for this particular system, both eigenvalues are positive. The dominant eigenvalue is the one with the greatest magnitude.

Now, since the solutions become parallel to the straight-line solution containing the vector ${v}_{1}$ as they move away from the origin, the dominant eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}.$

Therefore, ${\lambda }_{1}>{\lambda }_{2}>0.$

EXPLANATION

The straight-line solutions of the system have the form c1eλ1t[21]andc2eλ2t[−11].

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to v1=[21] has the equation y=12x, as shown below.

The tangents along this line are pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form c1eλ1t[21] must approach infinity as t→∞. So, we must have λ1>0.

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to v1=[−11] has the equation y=−x, as shown below.

The tangents along this line are pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form c2eλ2t[−11] must approach infinity as t→∞. So, we must have λ2>0.

So, for this particular system, both eigenvalues are positive. The dominant eigenvalue is the one with the greatest magnitude.

Now, since the solutions become parallel to the straight-line solution containing the vector v1 as they move away from the origin, the dominant eigenvalue is λ1.

Therefore, λ1>λ2>0.
